metadata.title: RICE-HUSK BIOCHAR AND TRICHODERMA FORTIFICATION MODULATE THE CHEMICAL AND MICROBIOLOGICAL PROFILES OF  ORGANIC-WASTE LIQUID FERTILIZER
metadata.description: Liquid organic fertilizer (LOF) derived from mixed organic residues may promote nutrient circularity; however, its chemical quality and microbial viability depend on formulation and fermentation conditions. This study assessed the effects of rice-husk biochar and Trichoderma spp. fortification on LOF produced from banana peel, pineapple peel, rabbit urine, and molasses in a passively aerated stacked-bucket system. A randomized complete block design included four treatments with four replicates: unfortified LOF (P1), Trichoderma alone (P2), 1% w/v biochar (P3), and biochar plus Trichoderma (P4). Chemical variables were analyzed by ANOVA followed by Tukey's HSD test at 5%, whereas microbial and metal data were interpreted descriptively. Fortification did not affect pH (7.20–7.22). P3 had the highest organic C (0.58%) and C/N ratio (5.92), whereas P4 had the highest total N (0.12%), P (0.22%), and K (0.62%). P2 had the highest total fungal count (7.2 × 10⁵ CFU mL⁻¹) and recoverable Trichoderma population (6.5 × 10⁵ CFU mL⁻¹); corresponding values in P4 were 3.8 × 10⁵ and 3.5 × 10⁵ CFU mL⁻¹. Co-fortification improved macronutrient profiles but did not maximize Trichoderma recovery from the liquid fraction. Further optimization and plant-based efficacy testing are required.
keywords: liquid organic fertilizer; organic waste; passive-aerobic fermentation; rice-husk biochar; Trichoderma

metadata.title: BRIDGING THE COMPUTATIONAL GAP: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A CUSTOM WEB CORPUS TOOL
metadata.description: The integration of corpus linguistics into Translation Studies (TS) is widely recognized as a methodological necessity for evaluating and improving automated translation systems. However, a significant software barrier persists: commercial platforms impose prohibitive subscription costs, while open-source Python libraries require advanced programming expertise. This paper details the software architecture and computational engineering of a custom-built, open-source web application designed to bridge this gap. Developed using the Flask microframework and integrating the spaCy Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipeline, the platform provides zero-installation access to advanced analytical features. The architectural design includes a multi-stage document ingestion pipeline capable of optical character recognition (OCR) for scanned PDFs, chunked processing for memory-efficient text parsing, and a JSON-based inverted index for rapid data retrieval. By engineering complex functionalities such as Parallel Concordancing, Corpus Query Language (CQL) parsing, and automated web-scraping within an intuitive graphical interface, this platform provides a highly scalable computational infrastructure for data-driven translation research.

data.title: BRIDGING THE COMPUTATIONAL GAP: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A CUSTOM WEB CORPUS TOOL

metadata.title: EFFECTIVE WAYS TO USE DEVICES OPERATING IN A MECHATRONICS SYSTEM
metadata.description:
The article presents the results of experimental studies of innovatively designed light traps for controlling and
monitoring the development stages of pest insects based on mechatronic light traps. The device, which operates on the
mechatronic system, automatically monitors insects during the day, as a result of which types of harmful insect populations
are studied. The mechanisms of the solar panel movement change depending on the movement of the sun have
been studied. When darkness falls, the device is activated using light sensors. The light lamp attracts flying pest insects
by affecting the light pathogen wavelength and calling them. The smell of the pheromone that kills the pest insects on
the high-voltage wire mesh attracts the pest insects to fly through the high-voltage wire mesh, the butterflies burn as a
result of contact and fall into the bag. When light falls, the sensors open the device. The solar panel is activated by the
movement of the sun, which drives the mechatronic system. The charging device is fully charged with energy. It has been
studied that the power of a solar battery depends on the semiconductor material, the design of the solar cell, and the
number of elements in the battery.

data.title: EFFECTIVE WAYS TO USE DEVICES OPERATING IN A MECHATRONICS SYSTEM

metadata.title: The network that learned to run itself
metadata.description: The limitations of traditional automation with scale and complexity have given rise to a powerful new concept - hyper-automation - Mostly for IT and cybersecurity areas. It is a system that allows machines to be self-managed and self-adaptive through AI, machine learning, and software orchestration, reducing human intervention. Streaming services, IoT sensors, and remote works are just some of the main drivers that bring about the need to shift traditional rule-based automation to proactive, self-regulating networks, which are enabled by real-time monitoring and decision-making like, for example, congestion prevention and resource allocation done autonomously by AIOps tools. So, 24x7 security, with minimum downtime and human error, is possible to achieve by organizations. Meanwhile, the reliance on autonomous systems creates important questions about trust responsibility accountability and Because of this, the necessity of effective oversight as well as the presence of highly trained personnel who are capable of handling these technologies will become paramount to the equation. Businesses that implement hyper-automation [1] well may end up far ahead of the competitors that still rely on manual processes. It just goes to show that as the network landscape evolves, the organizations that are going to thrive are the ones adopting hyper-automation at a deep level. In the end, getting on board with hyper-automation is not only a futuristic consideration, it is a requirement for organizations who desire to be competitive in the digital world.[14][15][16][17]

metadata.title: Promoting inclusive rural development: A mixed-methods evaluation of TEKAD's impact in eastern Indonesia
metadata.description:
Persistent rural disparities in Indonesia’s eastern provinces necessitate innovative, inclusive development approaches.

The Transformasi Ekonomi Kampung Terpadu (TEKAD) program, a partnership between the Indonesian

government and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), aims to transform rural

economies through participatory planning, micro-enterprise support, and enhanced financial and institutional

access. This study employs a sequential mixed-methods approach, analysing quantitative data from 698

households across 47 villages in ten regencies at Eastern Indonesia namely, Papua Island, Nusa Tenggara Timur

and Maluku, complemented by qualitative insights from interviews and observations. This research found that

the program’s outcomes exceed the targets for financial access and market access but underperformed in productivity,

technology adoption, institutional trust, and investment satisfaction, particularly in fisheries and regions

with weak governance. People with disabilities faced significant exclusion, highlighting deficiencies in

TEKAD’s Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) framework. The study reveals tensions between

decentralized development and implementation consistency, aligning with adaptive governance scholarship.

Recommendations include context-sensitive strategies, universal design principles, and integrated value-

chain planning to enhance equitable rural transformation in Indonesia and similar settings.

data.title: Promoting inclusive rural development: A mixed-methods evaluation of TEKAD's impact in eastern Indonesia

metadata.title: Replication package — Doing MOS and its alternatives well: a variance-decomposition guide for TTS perceptual evaluation
metadata.description: Replication package for the paper Doing MOS—and its alternatives—well: a variance-decomposition guide for TTS perceptual evaluation (Chevelu & Barbot, Univ. Rennes, CNRS, IRISA; Computer Speech & Language, Special Issue on the evaluation of speech and speech synthesis). It contains the code, frozen output tables and figures that reproduce every quantitative claim in the paper, organised by section: variance/CI experiments, the K=2 allocation penalty, the BTTF case study, the multi-edition Blizzard Challenge panorama, the corpus design census, and the AnytimeMonitor worked example. Redistributed Blizzard Challenge listening-test scores are included with attribution (no audio). The AnytimeMonitor controller driving Section 8 is released separately as the anytimemonitor software (linked). MIT licence.
